questions.prompt: What is the key advantage of a user-defined bridge network over the default bridge?

options.text: It provides automatic DNS, so containers can reach each other by container name

questions.explanation: On a user-defined bridge, containers resolve each other by name via built-in DNS. The default bridge supports communication only by IP address.

questions.prompt: Do two containers on the same network need a published port to communicate with each other?

options.text: No; publishing is only for reaching a container from the host or outside world

questions.explanation: Containers on the same network talk directly over the container port. You publish (-p) only what needs to be reachable from outside.

questions.prompt: How should one container refer to another for a reliable connection?

options.text: By the other container's IP address, hard-coded
By the other container's name on a shared user-defined network
By the host machine's public IP

questions.explanation: Use the container/service name on a shared user-defined network. Docker resolves the name via DNS, and names are stable while IPs can change.

questions.prompt: The network mode that gives a container no external networking at all is called ______. (one word)
questions.explanation: The none network mode leaves a container with only loopback and no external connectivity, useful for fully isolated tasks.

questions.prompt: Which statements about Docker networking are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: EXPOSE in a Dockerfile only documents a port; it does not open it
A container can be connected to more than one network
The default bridge resolves container names via DNS
Publishing with -p forwards a host port to a container port

questions.explanation: EXPOSE is documentation, containers can join multiple networks, and -p forwards a host port. Name resolution works on user-defined bridges, not the default bridge.

questions.prompt: Order these steps to run an app and database that talk by name.

items.text: The app connects to the database at hostname db

questions.explanation: Create the shared network, start both containers on it, and the app resolves the database by its container name db.
